state: "Claim for the lake house, policy SEA-3309127. We closed the cottage up at the end of the season like we always do. We shut the water off at the main valve, but we didn't drain the lines this year because the plumber we usually use retired and we hadn't found a new one. The heat was set to 50 when we left, at least that's what we set it to. Our neighbor across the road, who keeps an eye on the place, called on Monday to say he saw water coming out under the back door. When we got up there on Tuesday the house was freezing inside, the thermostat display was blank, and a pipe under the kitchen sink had split. There was water through the kitchen and into the family room, the floors are buckled, and the lower cabinets are swollen. The electric company told us there was a neighborhood outage over the weekend during the cold snap, but power came back on Sunday afternoon. Our furnace is oil and the tank still has oil in it, so we don't know why it wouldn't have come back on. We haven't been up there since we closed it. We've owned the cottage for eleven years and never had a problem like this. The furnace was serviced in the spring. There's a smart thermostat but the wifi account lapsed, so we couldn't see the temperature remotely. The neighbor says he last walked around the outside the week before and everything looked normal. "THREAD: Disability Parking Placard - Application DP-26-1187

[1] 2026-03-02, Motor Vehicle Division to applicant (Ines Carvalho): Your application for a permanent disability parking placard has been DENIED. Reason: the medical certification section was completed by a chiropractor. Under Rule 15.2 the certification must be completed by a physician (MD/DO), physician assistant, nurse practitioner, or podiatrist. You may request an administrative review within the period stated on this notice, or submit a new application with a valid certification.

[2] 2026-03-04, applicant to MVD: I don't understand. My chiropractor has treated my back for six years and knows my condition better than anyone. I can barely walk from the far end of the grocery lot. What am I supposed to do, pay for a new doctor visit just to sign a form?

"From: procurement@example.org
Subject: RFP - Regional distribution partner, Great Lakes network (response due Oct 31)

Hello,

Meridian Outdoor Supply is issuing a request for proposal for a 3PL partner to operate two regional distribution centres (Toledo and Grand Rapids) serving 140 retail doors and our e-commerce channel. Scope: inbound receiving from 35 domestic suppliers and two Asian ports via rail ramp, storage of roughly 9,000 SKUs with strong seasonality (camping and winter lines), store replenishment twice weekly, and e-commerce pick/pack/ship with same-day cut-off at 14:00. We expect peak volumes in November and May.

Budget: our board has approved a three-year operating budget for this programme; we will share the envelope with shortlisted vendors only. Timeline: shortlist by Nov 20, site visits in early December, contract award before Jan 15, go-live April 1 ahead of camping season.

Decision process: an evaluation committee chaired by our COO, Hector Blanco, with the VP Supply Chain and CFO. Final approval sits with the COO.

Mandatory requirements: WMS with EDI 856/940/945 support, SOC 2 Type II report, cold-weather yard operations, and at least one existing retail client with 100+ stores. Please include references.

Our incumbent's contract ends March 31; we are open to them re-bidding.

Please confirm your intent to bid by replying to this email. Attached: RFP_Meridian_3PL.pdf (42 pages), pricing template (xlsx).

Regards,
Nora Feld
Senior Procurement Manager

This email and any attachments are confidential and intended solely for the addressee. If you have received it in error, please notify the sender and delete it. Meridian Outdoor Supply is an equal-opportunity purchaser and encourages responses from diverse suppliers."

Subject: Window AC request - Unit 7E

Hello, I have multiple sclerosis and heat makes my symptoms much worse (my neurologist calls it Uhthoff's phenomenon: blurred vision, weakness in my legs, fatigue). Last summer my bedroom hit 86 degrees most nights. I'd like permission to install a window air conditioner in my bedroom window. I know the lease says no window units, so I'm asking for an exception because of my disability.

---
From: Parkside Residents Office
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 11:40

Hi Hannah, thank you for explaining. Lease §9.4 prohibits window-mounted air conditioners on all floors because units have fallen from upper-story windows at other properties and the building's insurer excludes that risk. Portable units vented through a window kit are allowed. Could a portable unit meet your need? We'd also like to understand what your doctor recommends.

---
From: Hannah Oduya
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 19:02

I tried a portable unit last summer, it could not keep up, and my bedroom window is a casement (it cranks outward) so the slider kit didn't seal. Attached is a letter from Dr. Priya Sandoval, my neurologist: 'Ms. Oduya has a neurological condition in which elevated body temperature worsens symptoms. ---
From: Maintenance Supervisor (internal note, forwarded to office)
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 07:55

For 7E: we can cut a plexiglass insert for the casement so a portable unit's exhaust hose seals properly; we did this in 3E last year and it holds temp fine in a bedroom that size. A 14,000 BTU dual-hose portable would be my pick. A window unit on 7 over the entry walkway is exactly what the insurer is worried about.

---
Lease §9.4 (excerpt): Window-mounted air conditioners are prohibited in all units. Portable air conditioners vented through a manufacturer or management-approved window kit are permitted, and management will fabricate a kit for non-standard windows on request at no charge.
